tb21_profile.skill: Diff two circular plasmid sequences (allowing for rotation) to localise the desired insertion, then design back-to-back Q5 SDM primer pairs whose 5' tails carry the insert and whose annealing portions alone satisfy 15-45nt / 58-72C / pair dTm<=5, with oligotm as the oracle and the pair count minimised.
tb21_profile.domain: Molecular biology: site-directed mutagenesis, circular plasmids, PCR primers, reverse complement, primer3 oligotm, FASTA.
tb21_profile.task_form: Implement-from-spec constrained design, plus a recover-the-difference step between two given sequences; strict output-file contract.

notes: Near-sibling of dna-assembly and the candidate pools overlap heavily, so the two files share several ids - intentionally. Ranking differs: dna-insert additionally needs a sequence-diff/alignment step and circular-coordinate handling, so Smith-Waterman (scientific-computing_20260414_091921_004), the two circular-plasmid CalibForge tasks, and the alignment-based TMax tasks rise while restriction-enzyme tasks fall. Terminal-Lego-15k again has essentially nothing: only task_08980 and task_09030 mention DNA in the entire 15k corpus, and only task_09030 (circular rotation identity) is a real conceptual hit. Recursive-Task-Synthesis offers four bio entries, two of them near-duplicate wgsim tasks, all `absent`. TerminalWorld's strongest bio candidates are FREE and were excluded from final_top10. SWE-Smith contributes only alignment-algorithm repairs; SWE-Rebench only the three cogent3 issues. Final list is 6 CalibForge + 4 TMax; CalibForge's molecular-biology block clearly beats the v1 pool here.
